warudo.connected.description: Runs when Cuebot connects to Warudo.

warudo.disconnected.description: Runs when the connection to Warudo drops, for example because you closed it.

warudo.toggleChanged.description: Runs when an "On Stream Deck Toggle" node in Warudo turns on or off, whoever flipped it (Cuebot, a Stream Deck or Warudo itself).

fields.receiver: Only react to these Receiver Names. Separate several with commas. Leave empty for any.
fields.state: Only react when it turns On, only when it turns Off, or Any.

variables.receiver: The Receiver Name of the toggle
variables.value: True when it is now on

warudo.trigger.description: Runs a Warudo blueprint: every "On Stream Deck Trigger" node with this Receiver Name starts, for example to throw props or play an animation.

fields.receiver: The Receiver Name typed into the node in Warudo. Capital letters matter. If the open scene has no such node, Cuebot still sends it and writes a warning to the log.

warudo.toggle.description: Turns a Warudo toggle on or off: "On Stream Deck Toggle" nodes with this Receiver Name run their "If Yes" path (turned on) or their "If No" path (turned off), for example to show or hide an accessory.

fields.receiver: The Receiver Name typed into the node in Warudo.
fields.state: On, Off, or Toggle (the opposite of now). Warudo can only flip a toggle, so for On and Off Cuebot first asks Warudo for its state when it does not know it, and skips the flip when it is already right.

variables.warudo.toggle: True when Warudo reports it is now on, false when off (empty if Warudo did not report a state, for example because no node has this Receiver Name)

warudo.message.description: Sends text to Warudo: "On Stream Deck Message" nodes with this Receiver Name start and pass the text on, for example a viewer's name to show.

fields.receiver: The Receiver Name typed into the node in Warudo.
fields.message: The text to send. It can use %arguments% like %user%.

warudo.getToggle.description: Reads whether a Warudo toggle ("On Stream Deck Toggle" node) is on, asking Warudo for its current state, then runs the On or the Off branch. An unknown toggle runs Off.

fields.receiver: The Receiver Name typed into the node in Warudo.

variables.warudo.toggle: True when it is on, false when off (empty if Warudo does not know this toggle)

warudo.webSocketMessage.description: Sends text to Warudo's own WebSocket port (19190): every "On WebSocket Message Received" node in the open scene starts with it. This needs no Stream Deck node and no Stream Deck connection, only Warudo running.

fields.message: The text to send. It can use %arguments% like %user%, and can be JSON if your blueprint parses it.
